subject: physics
title: States of matter and density
key_idea: In the particle model, a solid, liquid or gas is described by how its particles are arranged and how they move. Density is mass divided by volume. Solids and liquids are dense because their particles are close together. Gases are not.

blocks.text: Everything is made of tiny particles (atoms or molecules). The particle model explains solids, liquids and gases by how these particles are arranged and how they move.

rows: More kinetic energy than a solid

items: A solid keeps its shape because its particles are held in fixed positions.
A liquid flows because its particles can move past each other.
A gas spreads out to fill its container because its particles are far apart and move freely.
Heating a substance gives its particles more kinetic energy.
Solids: regular pattern, fixed positions, particles vibrate.
Liquids: random arrangement, touching, particles move freely.
Gases: far apart, random, fast, with negligible forces between particles.

sections.heading: Density and how to calculate it

blocks.text: Density tells you how much mass is packed into each unit of volume. This section covers the equation, its units and how to use it.

items.meaning: The mass of a material in each unit of volume.
The amount of space an object takes up.

blocks.label: Density
where: density, ρ, in kilograms per metre cubed, kg/m³
volume, V, in metres cubed, m³

items: Density is often given in g/cm³ as well. 1 g/cm³ = 1000 kg/m³.
To find the mass: m = ρ × V.
To find the volume: V = m ÷ ρ.
1 cm³ = 0.000 001 m³, so convert cm³ to m³ before using kg/m³.

items.text: Use kg and m³ if the density is in kg/m³. For example, 50 cm³ = 0.000 050 m³.
m = ρ × V or V = m ÷ ρ.
A 6.0 kg block of volume 0.0030 m³ has a density of 6.0 ÷ 0.0030 = 2000 kg/m³.
Write kg/m³ or g/cm³ with the answer.

sections.heading: Why the states differ in density

blocks.text: A material's density depends on the mass of its particles and on how closely they are packed. The state of a material changes the packing but not the mass.

items: In a solid, particles are touching in a regular arrangement, so a solid is usually very dense.
In a liquid, particles are also touching but are arranged randomly, so a liquid is only slightly less dense than the solid.
In a gas, particles are far apart. The same mass takes up a much larger volume, so a gas is far less dense.
Density order, lowest first: gas, liquid, solid. Water is an exception, because ice is less dense than liquid water.

blocks.text: When a substance changes state, its particles are the same and are not lost. The mass stays the same, but the volume changes, so the density changes.

rows: Solid melts to a liquid (most substances)

blocks.text: A material full of air pockets, such as pumice, has a lower density than solid rock, because the air adds volume but very little mass.

items: A gas is much less dense than a solid or liquid because its particles are far apart.
Mass is conserved in a change of state. The volume changes, so the density changes.
Density depends on the mass of the particles and on how they are arranged.

checks.q: Describe the arrangement and movement of the particles in a solid.
checks.a: The particles are in a regular pattern, touching, in fixed positions. They vibrate about these positions.

checks.q: Explain why a gas is much less dense than a solid of the same substance.
checks.a: The particles in a gas are far apart, but in a solid they are close together. The same mass takes up a much larger volume in a gas.

checks.q: An object has a mass of 6.0 kg and a volume of 0.0030 m³. Calculate its density.
A rock has a density of 2.7 g/cm³. Give its density in kg/m³.

exam_phrases: the particles are in fixed positions

mistakes.wrong: Using a volume of 0.44 in the equation when the volume is 0.44 cm³ and the density is in kg/m³.
mistakes.right: Convert first: 0.44 cm³ = 4.4 × 10⁻⁷ m³. The conversion earns its own mark.

mistakes.wrong: Working out the volume of a cube of width 18.45 mm as 18.45 × 3.
mistakes.right: Volume of a cube = width × width × width. V = (18.45 × 10⁻³)³ = 6.28 × 10⁻⁶ m³.

mistakes.wrong: Giving 6 487 000 000 kg when the question asks for the answer in standard form.
mistakes.right: The last mark needs standard form: 6.487 × 10⁹ kg.

worked_example.question: The density of a ring was 21 500 kg/m³. The volume of the ring was 0.44 cm³. Calculate the mass of the ring. Give your answer in kg.
worked_example.tip: One mark each for the unit conversion, the substitution, the rearrangement and the answer.

exam_phrases: particles in solid in regular arrangement but particles in liquid are randomly arranged
particles in a liquid have more (kinetic) energy (than in a solid)

mistakes.wrong: Giving the density as 2680 with no unit.
mistakes.right: The unit is a separate mark. Write 2680 kg/m³ (or 2.68 g/cm³).

mistakes.wrong: Writing only that particles in a liquid move freely, when asked for differences between a solid and a liquid.
mistakes.right: Compare them. In a solid the particles vibrate in fixed positions in a regular arrangement. In a liquid they move freely and are randomly arranged.

mistakes.wrong: Writing 2.68 kg/cm³ because the mass was in kg and the volume was in m³.
mistakes.right: Use a consistent unit. kg with m³ gives kg/m³, and g with cm³ gives g/cm³.

worked_example.question: An object has a mass of 7.22 × 10⁻² kg and a volume of 2.69 × 10⁻⁵ m³. Calculate the density, ρ, of the object. Use the equation ρ = m / V. State the unit.
answer_points: ρ = 2680 (any value that rounds to 2680, such as 2684, or 2.68 × 10³)
worked_example.tip: One mark each for the substitution, the evaluation and the unit.

exam_phrases: density is less than the density of water

mistakes.wrong: Density depends on the position on Earth or the specific heat capacity.
mistakes.right: Density depends on the mass of the particles and the particle arrangement.

mistakes.wrong: Cube B has the same density as cube A, because they have the same volume.
mistakes.right: Density = mass ÷ volume. Cube B has ten times the mass in the same volume, so its density is ten times larger.

mistakes.wrong: Choose carbon fibre for the toy boat because it has the highest density.
mistakes.right: A solid boat floats if its density is less than the density of water (1000 kg/m³). Choose pine, which has the lowest density.

worked_example.question: One polystyrene block has a density of 50 kg/m³. The mass of the block is 0.60 kg. Calculate the volume of the block.
worked_example.tip: The second mark is for rearranging and substituting. 1.2 × 10 to any other power scores 2 marks.
